catalog.title: Use an intentional routing method
catalog.summary: Each queue should use a routing method explicitly selected for its interaction type and operating model.
catalog.why_it_matters: Routing method selection governs how interactions are assigned and materially affects fairness, skill matching, and service performance.
catalog.recommended_state: Routing method is documented and intentionally selected rather than inherited or left unreviewed.
catalog.anti_pattern: Queues use default or inherited routing without review.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes reference Standard ACD, Predictive, Preferred Agent, Bullseye, and Conditional Group routing.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect queue configuration and verify routing method exists and is documented in approved operating standards.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag queues missing approved routing metadata or using deprecated/unapproved routing methods.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Review each queue and explicitly confirm its routing method.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Inventory all queues, compare configured routing methods to approved standards, and document the business rationale for each exception.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Routing changes can affect assignment behavior; review during a controlled change window.
evidence_examples: Queue export showing routing method
Change ticket documenting rationale
catalog.sample_bad_state: Queue routing method is inherited or unknown.
catalog.sample_good_state: Queue is documented as Bullseye routing for tiered skill escalation.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some legacy queues may be intentionally frozen pending migration.
exceptions: Temporary exception during migration or decommissioning.

catalog.title: Change scoring only when the queue is empty
catalog.summary: Queue scoring methods should be set at creation time or changed only when no interactions are waiting.
catalog.why_it_matters: Changing scoring during an active backlog can produce unexpected assignment order.
catalog.recommended_state: Scoring changes occur only during no-backlog windows or controlled creation events.
catalog.anti_pattern: Changing scoring while interactions are already waiting in queue.
catalog.source_notes: Source explicitly notes scoring changes should occur at creation or when queue has no waiting interactions.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare queue routing/scoring change timestamps to queue backlog intervals from metrics or audit logs.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag changes where scoring update time overlaps periods with waiting interactions.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Move routing scoring changes to empty-queue windows.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review scoring change history, identify overlap with active queue backlog, and reschedule future changes during maintenance or no-volume windows.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Reverting scoring may change assignment ordering; coordinate with operations.
evidence_examples: Audit log entry for routing change
Queue metric showing active waiting count at same time
catalog.sample_bad_state: Scoring changed at 10:15 while 18 interactions were waiting.
catalog.sample_good_state: Scoring changed during pre-open window with zero backlog.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Historical backlog reconstruction may be approximate if metrics retention is incomplete.
exceptions: Emergency change approved during live incident.

catalog.title: Use skills only where the routing model benefits from them
catalog.summary: Skill tags and ratings should reflect real expertise and support the queue's routing strategy.
catalog.why_it_matters: Inflated or stale skill models create routing noise and false precision.
catalog.recommended_state: Skills are current, limited in scope, and tied to actual routing requirements.
catalog.anti_pattern: Overuse of skills with weak governance or no operational effect.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes describe skill tags and ratings as inputs to some routing methods.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review queue routing methods and compare configured skills to queue requirements and skill governance standards.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag skills not referenced by any queue logic or with extreme sprawl.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Trim unused or low-value skills.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Map each configured skill to a routing use case, remove stale skill assignments, and normalize rating practices.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Skill removal can affect staffing coverage; validate before changes.
evidence_examples: Skill inventory report
Queue routing design documentation
catalog.sample_bad_state: Agents have dozens of skills with no routing dependence.
catalog.sample_good_state: Only business-relevant skills are assigned and reviewed quarterly.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some queues intentionally keep rarely used specialty skills for surge or exception routing.
exceptions: Regulatory or language coverage skills retained for contingency.

catalog.title: Align wrap-up codes to the queue division
catalog.summary: Wrap-up codes assigned to a queue should belong to the same division where possible.
catalog.why_it_matters: Division-aligned wrap-up codes improve report clarity and reduce ambiguous reporting.
catalog.recommended_state: Queue wrap-up codes are division-consistent and intentionally curated.
catalog.anti_pattern: Queues use mixed or unrelated divisional wrap-up codes.
catalog.source_notes: Source notes recommend adding divisional codes to queues for better reporting.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare queue division to associated wrap-up code divisions.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag queues with cross-division wrap-up associations unless approved.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Align wrap-up codes to the queue's division.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review all queue-to-wrap-up mappings, replace unrelated divisional codes, and document exceptions for shared service queues.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Changing wrap-up catalogs affects reporting continuity; retain mapping history.
evidence_examples: Queue wrap-up assignment export
Division metadata
catalog.sample_bad_state: Finance queue uses wrap-up codes from unrelated service divisions.
catalog.sample_good_state: Queue wrap-up codes are owned by the same division as the queue.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Shared service queues may intentionally use cross-division catalogs.
exceptions: Shared services with approved common wrap-up taxonomy.

catalog.title: Implement explicit rate-limit handling
catalog.summary: Clients should inspect rate-limit responses and apply controlled backoff on throttling.
catalog.why_it_matters: Ignoring rate-limit behavior increases failure rates and amplifies instability.
catalog.recommended_state: Clients retry with bounded backoff and observability around throttling.
catalog.anti_pattern: Immediate retries or no retry strategy after 429 responses.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes mention controlled backoff intervals such as 3, 9, and 27 seconds.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect client code or integration behavior for 429 handling and retry telemetry.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag integrations that emit repeated 429s without exponential or policy-based backoff.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Add bounded retry logic for 429 responses.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Implement retry handling that inspects returned limit metadata, applies bounded backoff, and emits telemetry for sustained throttling.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Retry logic changes can alter throughput and request timing; test under load.
evidence_examples: Client code snippet with retry handler
Log sample showing bounded backoff after 429
catalog.sample_bad_state: Client retries immediately on every 429.
catalog.sample_good_state: Client backs off and logs limit type and retry decision.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Low-volume integrations may rarely hit limits, making runtime evidence sparse.
exceptions: None for production integrations.

catalog.title: Prefer notifications over polling for state changes
catalog.summary: Use subscription or notification mechanisms for asynchronous state changes where supported.
catalog.why_it_matters: Polling increases request volume and delays detection of changes.
catalog.recommended_state: Async workflows use notifications first and polling only as a fallback.
catalog.anti_pattern: Continuous polling for campaign or workflow state changes when notifications are available.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes recommend notifications rather than polling for campaign stop-state changes.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review integration design and runtime patterns for repeated state polling to endpoints that have event topics.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag high-frequency polling when event subscription support exists.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Replace polling with notifications where supported.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Identify polled workflows, map them to available notification topics, subscribe to those topics, and retain minimal fallback polling only when necessary.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Notification pipelines require connection reliability and reconnect handling.
evidence_examples: Polling trace logs
Subscription design documentation
catalog.sample_bad_state: Integration polls every 5 seconds for stop-state changes.
catalog.sample_good_state: Integration subscribes to events and polls only on reconnect recovery.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Fallback polling may be temporarily acceptable during migration.
exceptions: Short-term compatibility bridge during eventing rollout.

catalog.title: Use bulk endpoints for multi-record operations
catalog.summary: Bulk endpoints should be preferred for large-scale operations where supported.
catalog.why_it_matters: Bulk operations reduce request count and improve throughput.
catalog.recommended_state: High-volume workflows use bulk APIs instead of repeated single-record operations.
catalog.anti_pattern: Serial single-record calls at scale.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes explicitly recommend bulk endpoints for multiple contacts.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect high-volume workflows and compare endpoint usage to bulk-capable alternatives.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag repeated object-by-object calls where a bulk equivalent exists.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Use bulk APIs for high-volume workflows.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Identify repetitive single-object loops, replace them with supported bulk requests, and validate paging and error handling for partial failures.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Bulk operations may require different error handling and retry semantics.
evidence_examples: Request count analysis
Code diff replacing loops with bulk calls
catalog.sample_bad_state: Thousands of sequential single-contact updates.
catalog.sample_good_state: Batch operations use the supported bulk endpoint with error partitioning.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some endpoints may not offer bulk equivalents.
exceptions: Low-volume administrative scripts.

catalog.title: Request the minimum necessary OAuth scope
catalog.summary: Applications should request only the scopes required for their function.
catalog.why_it_matters: Excess scopes increase blast radius and violate least-privilege design.
catalog.recommended_state: OAuth clients request only justified scopes and review them periodically.
catalog.anti_pattern: Overbroad scopes granted for convenience.
catalog.source_notes: Research included OAuth scopes and least-privilege access themes.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare granted scopes against documented client purpose and endpoint usage.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag clients with scopes not tied to documented use cases.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Trim OAuth scopes to the minimum required.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review each OAuth client, map scopes to actual functionality, remove unused scope grants, and require approval for elevated scope changes.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Scope reductions can break clients; test application behavior before production rollout.
evidence_examples: OAuth client export
Function-to-scope mapping document
catalog.sample_bad_state: Read/write admin scopes granted to a read-only reporting app.
catalog.sample_good_state: Client uses only scoped read access required for reporting.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some vendor apps request broad scopes pending roadmap reduction.
exceptions: Temporarily approved vendor limitation with compensating controls.

catalog.title: Design BYOC Premises Edge redundancy as N+1
catalog.summary: Edge deployments should retain sufficient capacity if one active Edge fails.
catalog.why_it_matters: N+1 design preserves call continuity during Edge failure or outage.
catalog.recommended_state: Site design supports expected load with one active Edge unavailable.
catalog.anti_pattern: No spare capacity for Edge failure.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes explicitly describe N+1 redundancy for BYOC Premises Edge.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare Edge count and call capacity to peak expected concurrency under single-failure conditions.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag sites where remaining capacity after one Edge failure is below expected concurrent load.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Add or resize Edge capacity to meet N+1.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Model peak concurrency, subtract one active Edge from the design, and ensure the remaining capacity still meets the expected operating threshold.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Topology changes require planned telephony change windows.
evidence_examples: Capacity spreadsheet
Site topology diagram
catalog.sample_bad_state: Two Edges are required for normal load with no spare margin.
catalog.sample_good_state: Site remains within safe utilization after losing one Edge.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Small pilot sites may intentionally run without full redundancy.
exceptions: Documented low-criticality pilot or lab site.

catalog.title: Ensure phones have primary and secondary Edge registration paths
catalog.summary: Managed phones should be able to fail over between primary and secondary Edge assignments.
catalog.why_it_matters: Single-Edge dependency increases the chance of local phone service interruption.
catalog.recommended_state: Phone registration supports primary and secondary Edge resilience.
catalog.anti_pattern: Phones depend effectively on one Edge path.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes describe primary and secondary Edge assignments and rapid failover behavior.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect phone and site redundancy configuration for primary and secondary registration paths.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag phones or sites lacking effective redundant Edge registration.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Configure primary and secondary Edge paths.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review site-level Edge redundancy, ensure phone assignments participate correctly, and test failover behavior in a controlled manner.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Phone reassignment can briefly affect registration.
evidence_examples: Phone assignment export
Failover test record
catalog.sample_bad_state: Phone group is pinned to a single Edge path.
catalog.sample_good_state: Phones fail over to secondary Edge during primary outage testing.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some analog or legacy devices may not behave identically to managed phones.
exceptions: Legacy endpoint class under migration plan.

catalog.title: Combine only compatible Edge capacity classes
catalog.summary: Edge redundancy designs should use compatible Edge capacity classes.
catalog.why_it_matters: Incompatible capacity mixes can undermine redundancy assumptions.
catalog.recommended_state: Edges grouped for resilience are of compatible capacity class.
catalog.anti_pattern: Mixed incompatible Edge sizes in one redundancy scheme.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes call out compatible hardware classes for redundancy.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare Edge model/capacity class across each site redundancy set.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag unsupported or mismatched capacity-class combinations.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Align redundant Edge hardware classes.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review site redundancy groups, replace or reclassify unsupported combinations, and update capacity planning assumptions.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Hardware or topology changes should be staged.
evidence_examples: Edge hardware inventory
Redundancy matrix
catalog.sample_bad_state: A site mixes incompatible Edge classes in one failover group.
catalog.sample_good_state: Redundant Edges are within the supported compatibility set.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Inventory naming can obscure true compatibility classes.

catalog.title: Keep inter-Edge latency and jitter very low
catalog.summary: Inter-Edge network quality should support reliable failover and voice stability.
catalog.why_it_matters: High latency or jitter degrades failover behavior and voice experience.
catalog.recommended_state: Inter-Edge latency remains under approved thresholds and jitter stays minimal.
catalog.anti_pattern: Network quality between redundant Edges exceeds design targets.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes mention sub-10ms latency and under-1ms jitter targets.
catalog.detection_strategy: Measure network quality between Edge peers and compare against approved thresholds.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag sites where latency or jitter breaches design limits.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Reduce latency and jitter between redundant Edges.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Investigate WAN path quality, QoS policy, and physical topology; re-route or optimize the path to restore design targets.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Network changes can affect other services; coordinate with network engineering.
evidence_examples: Latency monitoring graph
Jitter test output
catalog.sample_bad_state: Inter-Edge latency averages 28ms with bursty jitter.
catalog.sample_good_state: Inter-Edge path remains stable within approved thresholds.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Short spikes may not indicate chronic design failure.
exceptions: Temporary degradation during provider incident.

catalog.title: Build flows for the organization, not by blindly adopting examples
catalog.summary: Example flows should be references only; production flows should be tailored to the organization's routing needs.
catalog.why_it_matters: Generic examples omit organization-specific controls, schedules, and routing expectations.
catalog.recommended_state: Flows are organization-specific and documented.
catalog.anti_pattern: Minimal edits to sample flows used in production.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes recommend building your own flow rather than using example flows directly.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review flow metadata and documentation for sample-derived content with missing local design artifacts.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag production flows lacking organization-specific ownership, naming, or schedule alignment.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Replace sample-based flows with tailored production designs.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review all sample-derived flows, document business-specific requirements, and refactor them into maintained production artifacts.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Flow updates require validation and publish controls.
evidence_examples: Flow export
Design note showing business-specific routing decisions
catalog.sample_bad_state: Production flow closely mirrors a sample without organization-specific controls.
catalog.sample_good_state: Flow has documented purpose, schedules, error handling, and owner.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some very simple utility flows may legitimately remain close to template patterns.
exceptions: Lab or demo flows.

catalog.title: Use distinct, descriptive names for flows, prompts, and states
catalog.summary: Names should be stable, descriptive, and not duplicative within type constraints.
catalog.why_it_matters: Clear naming improves maintenance, troubleshooting, and reporting.
catalog.recommended_state: Naming conventions are documented and consistently applied.
catalog.anti_pattern: Generic names such as Main, Test, or Copy 2 used in production artifacts.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes emphasize distinctive labels and non-duplicative names within type constraints.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect names against naming standards and duplicate-pattern heuristics.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag generic or duplicate-like names in production objects.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Apply clear naming conventions to Architect artifacts.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Define a naming standard using service, purpose, environment, and lifecycle markers; rename ambiguous production artifacts to match it.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Renaming can affect references in related documentation or deployment scripts.
evidence_examples: Flow inventory with duplicate-like names
Naming standard document
catalog.sample_bad_state: Multiple flows named Main or Test in production.
catalog.sample_good_state: Names identify business unit, purpose, and environment clearly.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some shared utility prompts may use short names intentionally.
exceptions: Sandbox-only artifacts.

catalog.title: Make schedule groups timezone-explicit and routing-aware
catalog.summary: Schedule groups should use explicit timezone handling and map cleanly to open, closed, holiday, and emergency routing.
catalog.why_it_matters: Hidden timezone assumptions can send interactions to the wrong routing path.
catalog.recommended_state: Schedules and schedule groups have explicit timezone ownership and clear routing outcomes.
catalog.anti_pattern: Implicit or undocumented timezone assumptions in routing schedules.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes discuss schedules, schedule groups, time zones, and open/closed or emergency routing.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect schedule groups for explicit timezone metadata and alignment with target routing outcomes.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag groups with missing timezone documentation or mismatched route targets.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Document and normalize schedule group timezones.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review all schedule groups, confirm explicit timezone ownership, verify holiday and emergency paths, and remove ambiguous route dependencies.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Schedule changes can affect live routing; coordinate change timing carefully.
evidence_examples: Schedule group export
Call flow route map
catalog.sample_bad_state: A schedule group uses inherited assumptions and routes incorrectly during DST changes.
catalog.sample_good_state: Schedule groups include explicit timezone control and verified route targets.
catalog.review_cadence: Before seasonal time changes and quarterly
catalog.false_positive_notes: Global follow-the-sun models may intentionally split logic across multiple schedule groups.
exceptions: Documented regional override pattern.

catalog.title: Use validation, versioning, and check-in/check-out discipline
catalog.summary: Flow lifecycle controls should be part of routine change management.
catalog.why_it_matters: Lifecycle discipline reduces drift and accidental production changes.
catalog.recommended_state: Flows are validated, versioned, and changed through a controlled process.
catalog.anti_pattern: Direct ad hoc edits to production flows without lifecycle controls.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes mention validation, versioning, and collaboration controls such as check in/check out.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review change process evidence for validation and publish discipline.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag flows changed without recorded validation or review evidence.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Adopt controlled lifecycle management for Architect flows.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Require validation before publish, preserve version history, and use documented promotion practices for production changes.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Lifecycle enforcement may slow emergency changes unless an exception path exists.
evidence_examples: Publish history
Change ticket or review record
catalog.sample_bad_state: Production flow changed directly with no recorded review.
catalog.sample_good_state: Flow change includes validation evidence and traceable publish history.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Legacy flows may lack older history even if current process is sound.
exceptions: Emergency incident response with after-action review.

catalog.title: Default to least privilege
catalog.summary: Users and integrations should receive only the permissions required for their function.
catalog.why_it_matters: Overprivileged access increases operational and security risk.
catalog.recommended_state: Access grants are role-aligned and reviewed regularly.
catalog.anti_pattern: Broad permissions granted for convenience or speed.
catalog.source_notes: Least privilege is explicitly called out in the source synthesis.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare granted permissions to documented job or application function.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag users or clients with permissions not justified by role or use case.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Reduce access to the least required set.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review permission grants by role and application purpose, remove nonessential permissions, and require documented approval for elevated access.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Privilege reduction can interrupt unsupported workflows; validate use cases first.
evidence_examples: Role assignment report
Access review record
catalog.sample_bad_state: Routine admins hold broad privileges unrelated to their duties.
catalog.sample_good_state: Access grants match documented role responsibilities.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Temporary project access may appear excessive if review data is missing.
exceptions: Time-bound approved elevation with expiration.

catalog.title: Prefer custom roles over broad admin grants
catalog.summary: Use custom roles instead of Master Admin when narrower access will satisfy the need.
catalog.why_it_matters: Master Admin grants create unnecessary blast radius.
catalog.recommended_state: Custom roles are used for bounded administrative tasks.
catalog.anti_pattern: Master Admin is assigned for convenience.
catalog.source_notes: Source synthesis explicitly contrasted custom roles with broad administrative grants.
catalog.detection_strategy: Identify users with Master Admin and compare their functions to available custom-role alternatives.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag Master Admin holders outside the approved break-glass population.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Replace broad admin grants with scoped custom roles.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review each Master Admin assignment, map actual tasks to granular permissions, create or refine custom roles, and reserve Master Admin for tightly controlled break-glass use.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Role substitution should be tested against administrative workflows.
evidence_examples: Role assignment list
Break-glass policy
catalog.sample_bad_state: Several daily operators hold Master Admin for routine work.
catalog.sample_good_state: Only documented emergency accounts retain broad admin rights.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Inherited legacy assignments may remain until a role redesign is complete.
exceptions: Approved emergency-only accounts.

catalog.title: Minimize role sprawl
catalog.summary: Keep the role catalog small, purposeful, and understandable.
catalog.why_it_matters: Role sprawl makes access review difficult and obscures intent.
catalog.recommended_state: Role catalog is curated and redundant roles are merged or retired.
catalog.anti_pattern: Large numbers of near-duplicate roles with unclear ownership.
catalog.source_notes: Role sprawl minimization was included in the source synthesis.
catalog.detection_strategy: Analyze role catalog size, overlap, and assignment density.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag low-use or overlapping roles for consolidation review.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Consolidate redundant roles.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review role overlap, merge near-duplicates, assign ownership, and retire unused roles after validation.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Role consolidation can affect downstream assumptions; validate assignments carefully.
evidence_examples: Role overlap matrix
Unused role report
catalog.sample_bad_state: Dozens of roles differ by one or two permissions without clear purpose.
catalog.sample_good_state: Role catalog is small, documented, and actively maintained.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some temporary transitional roles may be expected during redesign.
exceptions: Time-bound transition roles.

catalog.title: Use division scoping deliberately
catalog.summary: Division access boundaries should mirror real administrative and operational boundaries.
catalog.why_it_matters: Division scoping is a core containment mechanism in Genesys Cloud.
catalog.recommended_state: Division grants are explicit, justified, and aligned to ownership.
catalog.anti_pattern: Broad division access granted without a clear operational boundary.
catalog.source_notes: Division-based control was highlighted in the source synthesis.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare division assignments to organizational ownership and job function.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag users or roles with division scope broader than their function requires.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Reduce division access to the appropriate scope.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review division assignments against organizational ownership, remove excess scope, and document approved cross-division responsibilities.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Division changes can affect visibility and admin workflows.
evidence_examples: Division assignment report
Org ownership matrix
catalog.sample_bad_state: Regional admins have global division access without business need.
catalog.sample_good_state: Division scope matches actual administrative boundaries.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Shared service administrators may require cross-division access.
exceptions: Documented shared service function.

catalog.title: Monitor resource utilization before limits become urgent
catalog.summary: Track telephony object consumption and act before warning or critical thresholds.
catalog.why_it_matters: Object-limit exhaustion creates avoidable deployment and operational blockers.
catalog.recommended_state: Telephony limits are tracked and reviewed against safe thresholds.
catalog.anti_pattern: Resource limits are checked only after failures or warnings.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes include explicit telephony object limits and warning bands.
catalog.detection_strategy: Collect object counts and compare them to the approved warning and critical thresholds.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag resources approaching threshold bands.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Track and forecast telephony limit consumption.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Inventory telephony objects, alert before threshold crossings, and plan capacity or cleanup before new deployments are blocked.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Cleanup actions can affect dependent objects; verify relationships before removal.
evidence_examples: Limit dashboard
Object count trend chart
catalog.sample_bad_state: Extension assignments are near limit with no forecast or cleanup plan.
catalog.sample_good_state: Capacity trends are monitored and reviewed proactively.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Short spikes due to staged migrations may be acceptable if planned.
exceptions: Time-bound migration wave with approved capacity plan.

catalog.title: Manage DID and extension assignments intentionally
catalog.summary: Assign DIDs and extensions using controlled ranges and clear ownership.
catalog.why_it_matters: Ad hoc assignment complicates support, growth, and troubleshooting.
catalog.recommended_state: DID and extension ownership is tracked and assignment patterns are standardized.
catalog.anti_pattern: Manual one-off addressing with weak ownership records.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes cover single and ranged DID or extension assignment patterns.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review DID and extension assignment inventories for gaps, collisions, or undocumented ownership.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag unowned, inconsistent, or overlapping assignment patterns.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Standardize DID and extension assignment practices.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Reserve structured ranges, document owners, reconcile gaps and overlaps, and apply a standard assignment policy for new numbers.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Address changes may affect user reachability and integrations.
evidence_examples: Number inventory export
Ownership spreadsheet
catalog.sample_bad_state: DIDs are assigned ad hoc with missing owner records.
catalog.sample_good_state: Number ranges are reserved and each assignment has an owner.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Legacy numbers may temporarily lack full metadata during cleanup.
exceptions: Historical inventory cleanup backlog.

catalog.title: Ensure group ring users have required addressing
catalog.summary: Users participating in group ring should have the DID or extension configuration required for alerting behavior.
catalog.why_it_matters: Incomplete addressing can create missed or inconsistent group ring alerts.
catalog.recommended_state: Group ring membership and user addressing are aligned.
catalog.anti_pattern: Users are added to group ring without valid telephony addressing.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes state group ring members must have DID or extension assignment for alerts.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare group ring memberships to user telephony addressing assignments.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag users in group ring without the required addressability.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Correct user addressing for group ring members.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review group ring membership, verify DID or extension requirements for each member, and fix missing assignments before relying on alerting behavior.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Number assignments may affect other routing paths.
evidence_examples: Group membership export
User telephony config
catalog.sample_bad_state: Group ring includes users with no assigned extension or DID.
catalog.sample_good_state: Every group ring user is properly addressable for alerts.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Behavior may vary by user station model or configuration state.
exceptions: Temporarily staged users pending activation.

catalog.title: Prefer CX as Code for repeatable configuration management
catalog.summary: Supported Genesys Cloud objects should be managed as code where repeatability matters.
catalog.why_it_matters: Code-based management improves consistency, traceability, and promotion discipline.
catalog.recommended_state: Repeatable configuration is represented in source-controlled artifacts.
catalog.anti_pattern: Manual-only production changes with no reproducible source artifact.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes and synthesis reference CX as Code and Terraform-based deployment practices.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review deployment workflows to determine whether supported objects are represented as code and promoted through version control.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag critical supported objects changed only manually in production.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Represent repeatable Genesys configuration as code.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Inventory supported objects, move repeatable configuration into source-controlled artifacts, and establish promotion workflows for changes.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Introducing IaC can expose undocumented manual drift that must be reconciled.
evidence_examples: Terraform repository
Change history tied to code review
catalog.sample_bad_state: Critical production flows are modified manually with no code representation.
catalog.sample_good_state: Changes are proposed in source control and promoted through a pipeline.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Not every Genesys object is equally suited to immediate code management.
exceptions: Unsupported object classes pending roadmap alignment.

catalog.title: Use CI/CD for promotion and validation
catalog.summary: Promotion between environments should be automated and validated where possible.
catalog.why_it_matters: Automation reduces drift and manual deployment error.
catalog.recommended_state: Changes move through validated CI/CD workflows before production.
catalog.anti_pattern: Environment changes are manually re-created without validation.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes reference CI/CD pipeline blueprints for Genesys Cloud deployments.

catalog.logic_hint: Flag manual promotion patterns for objects covered by supported automation.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Adopt validated CI/CD promotion pipelines.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Define environment promotion stages, include validation and review gates, and require pipeline execution for production deployment of managed artifacts.
