catalog.title: Use Terraform-backed workflows where supported
catalog.summary: Architect and related supported objects should use Terraform-backed deployment where practical.
catalog.why_it_matters: Terraform-backed workflows improve reviewability and rollback discipline.
catalog.recommended_state: Supported objects use Terraform or equivalent managed deployment workflows.
catalog.anti_pattern: Production changes are applied without reviewed declarative artifacts.
catalog.source_notes: Research notes mention Terraform-backed Architect deployment blueprints.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review repositories and deployment workflows for declarative infrastructure artifacts covering supported objects.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag supported objects changed outside the managed Terraform path.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Move supported deployments into Terraform-backed workflows.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Inventory supported object types, define declarative artifacts, validate state alignment, and enforce reviewed pipeline-based deploys for those artifacts.
catalog.rollback_considerations: State reconciliation is needed before strict Terraform enforcement.
evidence_examples: Terraform module
Plan/apply run record
catalog.sample_bad_state: Architect objects are updated manually with no plan or apply history.
catalog.sample_good_state: Supported objects are promoted with reviewed declarative changes.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Not all objects or teams will be ready for immediate full declarative management.
exceptions: Interim manual process for unsupported resources.

catalog.title: Agent scripts for predictive campaigns must include a Set Stage action
catalog.summary: Each outbound predictive campaign's agent script must contain at least one Set Stage action to enable accurate pre-dialing behavior.
catalog.why_it_matters: Without a Set Stage action the predictive algorithm cannot determine call completion state and falls back to power-dialing mode, eliminating the efficiency advantages of predictive dialing.
catalog.recommended_state: All predictive campaign agent scripts contain at least one Set Stage action mapped to call outcomes.
catalog.anti_pattern: Predictive campaign agent script has no Set Stage action, causing silent fallback to power dialing.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud predictive dialing best practices article: 'Make sure that the agent script that you select for the predictive campaign has at least one Set Stage action.' Without it, campaign defaults to power dialing behavior.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect agent scripts associated with predictive campaigns and verify at least one Set Stage action is present.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag predictive campaigns whose linked agent scripts contain no Set Stage action.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Add a Set Stage action to all predictive campaign agent scripts.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review each predictive campaign's assigned agent script. Ensure at least one Set Stage action exists and maps to logical call stage outcomes (connected, voicemail, no-answer). Republish and validate campaign behavior in a lower environment before activating.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Script changes take effect on publish; test in a sandbox campaign before applying to live production campaigns.
evidence_examples: Script export showing Set Stage action
Campaign config linking script to predictive dialing mode
catalog.sample_bad_state: Predictive campaign script contains only disposition wrap-up logic with no Set Stage action; campaign silently dials in power mode.
catalog.sample_good_state: Script has Set Stage actions at connected and terminal outcomes, enabling predictive pre-dialing.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Power dialing campaigns legitimately do not require Set Stage.
exceptions: Power dialing campaigns intentionally not using predictive mode.

catalog.title: Maintain at least 15 effective logged-in agents for predictive dialing
catalog.summary: Predictive dialing campaigns require a minimum of 15 effective agents (full-time equivalents) for the pacing algorithm to generate accurate predictions.
catalog.why_it_matters: Below 15 effective agents the statistical model degrades, producing inaccurate pacing and elevated abandon or idle rates. Agents shared across campaigns count fractionally toward each campaign's effective pool.
catalog.recommended_state: Each active predictive campaign has at least 15 effective agents logged in and available during the dialing window.
catalog.anti_pattern: Predictive campaign runs with fewer than 15 effective agents, or agent count is diluted by cross-campaign sharing without adjustment.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud predictive dialing best practices: 'Maintain at least 15 logged-in agents for algorithm accuracy. Agents logged into multiple campaigns count fractionally (e.g., 20 agents across 2 campaigns = 10 effective agents per campaign). Insufficient data compromises agent availability calculations.'
catalog.detection_strategy: Monitor agent availability and logged-in count during predictive campaign windows. Calculate effective FTE accounting for cross-campaign fractional shares.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag active predictive campaigns where effective agent count (after fractional cross-campaign share deduction) is below 15.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Ensure at least 15 effective agents are available during each predictive campaign window.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Audit agent assignments across concurrent predictive campaigns. Calculate effective FTE per campaign. Adjust schedules, reduce concurrent campaign count, or switch to power dialing if the minimum cannot be sustained.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Changing campaign mode or agent assignments mid-run may affect in-progress pacing.
evidence_examples: Real-time or historical agent adherence report
Campaign concurrent run schedule with effective FTE calculation
catalog.sample_bad_state: Predictive campaign runs with 8 agents shared across three concurrent campaigns, yielding under 3 effective agents per campaign.
catalog.sample_good_state: Campaign consistently has 20+ dedicated agents logged in throughout the dialing window.
catalog.review_cadence: Per campaign launch and ongoing daily monitoring
catalog.false_positive_notes: Campaigns intentionally run small may use power dialing mode instead.
exceptions: Small-volume pilot campaigns explicitly configured as power dialing.

catalog.title: Randomize outbound contact lists before campaign use
catalog.summary: Contact list order should be randomized to prevent geographic or demographic sorting from creating uneven dialing peaks and valleys.
catalog.why_it_matters: Lists sorted by area code, postal code, or last name concentrate similar contacts in sequence, producing dialing spikes followed by idle windows that degrade predictive pacing accuracy and abandon rate control.
catalog.recommended_state: Contact lists are randomized before each campaign run, either via Genesys Cloud built-in sorting or external pre-processing.
catalog.anti_pattern: Contact list exported from a CRM sorted by region or area code and uploaded without randomization.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud predictive dialing best practices: 'Randomize contact list order to maintain steady contact rates. Avoid geographic or demographic sorting, which creates peaks and valleys. Use external tools (SQL, Excel) or Genesys Cloud built-in sorting.'
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect contact list upload procedures and data ordering for obvious geographic or sequential patterns that would cause burst dialing.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag contact lists with sequential geographic patterns (all area codes ascending or all zip codes in order) that would create burst dialing behavior.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Apply randomization to all outbound contact lists before uploading.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Use Genesys Cloud contact list sorting or pre-process lists with SQL, Excel, or Python randomization. Document the randomization step in the campaign run-book and enforce it in the data preparation pipeline.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Re-sorting an active contact list may reset position and affect in-progress campaign record tracking.
evidence_examples: Contact list sample showing randomized record order
Campaign run-book step for list randomization
catalog.sample_bad_state: Contact list uploaded sorted by zip code, creating 200 consecutive calls to the same area code.
catalog.sample_good_state: Contact list shuffled randomly before each campaign run; step is documented in the run-book.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Geographically targeted campaigns may intentionally use geographic ordering for time-zone compliance.
exceptions: Geographically targeted campaigns with documented time-zone compliance requirements.

catalog.title: Enable agent auto-answer for predictive dialing campaigns
catalog.summary: Agent auto-answer must be enabled to minimize call delivery delay in predictive dialing environments.
catalog.why_it_matters: Manual answer introduces latency between call connection and agent pickup, increasing abandoned calls and degrading the customer experience in predictive dialing where calls are pre-dialed before the agent is free.
catalog.recommended_state: Auto-answer is enabled on queues serving predictive outbound campaigns.
catalog.anti_pattern: Agents must manually accept each connected call in a predictive campaign queue, increasing connection abandonment.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud predictive dialing best practices recommend enabling agent auto-answer to minimize call delivery delay and reduce campaign abandonment.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect queue configuration for auto-answer settings on queues associated with active predictive outbound campaigns.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag predictive campaign queues where auto-answer is not enabled.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Enable auto-answer on all queues serving predictive campaigns.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Locate all queues associated with active predictive campaigns. Enable auto-answer on those queues. Confirm agent station and headset readiness to avoid missed connections upon auto-answer.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Enabling auto-answer changes the agent experience; communicate the change and provide training before rollout.
evidence_examples: Queue config export showing auto-answer enabled
Campaign-to-queue association documentation
catalog.sample_bad_state: Predictive campaign queue has auto-answer disabled; agents must click to accept connected calls, causing abandons.
catalog.sample_good_state: Auto-answer enabled on outbound queue; calls connect to agents immediately upon predictive dial success.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some compliance workflows may require explicit agent acceptance before call connection.
exceptions: Regulatory requirement mandating explicit agent acceptance prior to call connection.

catalog.title: Use persistent connections for Polycom and WebRTC agents in outbound campaigns
catalog.summary: Persistent connections should be configured for agents using Polycom or WebRTC phones in outbound campaign environments to eliminate per-call session setup overhead.
catalog.why_it_matters: Non-persistent connections require a new session negotiation for each outbound call, adding latency between campaign call delivery and agent connection that is unacceptable in a predictive dialing environment.
catalog.recommended_state: All agents on Polycom or WebRTC phones participating in outbound campaigns have persistent connections configured on their station.
catalog.anti_pattern: Polycom or WebRTC agents in predictive campaigns without persistent connections, incurring per-call session setup latency.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud predictive dialing best practices recommend using persistent connections for Polycom and WebRTC phones to eliminate call setup latency in outbound campaign environments.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect station and phone configuration for agents in outbound campaign queues and verify persistent connection setting.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag Polycom or WebRTC agents in active outbound campaign queues without persistent connection enabled.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Enable persistent connections for outbound agents on Polycom or WebRTC phones.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Identify all agents participating in predictive campaigns who use Polycom or WebRTC stations. Enable persistent connection on each phone profile. Verify the configuration takes effect and monitor for session stability issues.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Changing station config affects active sessions; schedule during non-campaign hours.
evidence_examples: Station config export showing persistent connection enabled
Before/after call setup latency comparison for campaign agents
catalog.sample_bad_state: WebRTC agent in predictive campaign without persistent connection; noticeable delay on each connected call.
catalog.sample_good_state: All outbound campaign agents on Polycom or WebRTC phones have persistent connections active.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Not all phone types support persistent connections; absences on non-qualifying device types are not findings.
exceptions: Non-Polycom/WebRTC phone types where persistent connection is not applicable.

catalog.title: Never hardcode Genesys Cloud Terraform credentials in configuration files
catalog.summary: Genesys Cloud Terraform provider credentials (OAuth client ID, secret, region) must be supplied via environment variables or a secrets manager, never hardcoded in .tf or .tfvars files.
catalog.why_it_matters: Hardcoded credentials in source-controlled Terraform files are trivially exposed via repository history, build logs, and CI artifact storage. A leaked OAuth admin credential creates unrestricted platform access.
catalog.recommended_state: Credentials are sourced from GENESYSCLOUD_OAUTHCLIENT_ID, GENESYSCLOUD_OAUTHCLIENT_SECRET, and GENESYSCLOUD_REGION environment variables or an approved vault integration. No literal secrets appear in .tf or .tfvars files.
catalog.anti_pattern: OAuth client ID and secret appear as literal strings in provider blocks or variable defaults in Terraform files committed to source control.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud Terraform provider README instructs: 'Set credentials via environment variables rather than hardcoding them into configuration files: GENESYSCLOUD_OAUTHCLIENT_ID, GENESYSCLOUD_OAUTHCLIENT_SECRET, GENESYSCLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN, GENESYSCLOUD_REGION.'
catalog.detection_strategy: Scan Terraform files in source repositories for provider blocks containing literal credential strings or variable default values matching OAuth client ID or secret patterns.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag .tf or .tfvars files containing strings matching OAuth client credential patterns not sourced from environment variable references.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Move all Genesys Cloud Terraform credentials to environment variables or a vault.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Remove credential literals from all Terraform files. Configure GENESYSCLOUD_OAUTHCLIENT_ID, GENESYSCLOUD_OAUTHCLIENT_SECRET, and GENESYSCLOUD_REGION as pipeline secrets via vault or CI secret store. Rotate any previously exposed credentials. Add a pre-commit hook or SAST rule to prevent recurrence.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Credential rotation invalidates active sessions; schedule during low-activity windows.
evidence_examples: Provider block using environment variable references, no literals
Pipeline secret configuration showing vault or CI secret injection
catalog.sample_bad_state: provider block contains oauthclient_id = 'abc123-...' as a literal value in a committed Terraform file.
catalog.sample_good_state: Credentials sourced from pipeline-injected environment variables; no secrets in source control.
catalog.review_cadence: Per repository onboarding and quarterly secret rotation audit
catalog.false_positive_notes: Variable declarations with no default value and no literal assignment are acceptable placeholders.

catalog.title: Configure Terraform eventual consistency handling deliberately
catalog.summary: The Genesys Cloud Terraform provider's built-in consistency checker should be configured intentionally; disabling it in production silences real deployment failures.
catalog.why_it_matters: Genesys Cloud's API is eventually consistent. The consistency checker retries after apply to confirm resource state converges. Setting CONSISTENCY_CHECKS=0 entirely prevents those retries, which can hide real failures that would otherwise surface as errors.
catalog.recommended_state: Consistency checker is active in production pipelines with a deliberate retry count. Disabling the checker is documented, justified, and limited to non-production environments.
catalog.anti_pattern: CONSISTENCY_CHECKS=0 set globally across all environments without documented rationale, silencing consistency verification entirely.
catalog.source_notes: Terraform provider README: 'The provider includes a consistency checker addressing eventual consistency issues. Configure via BYPASS_CONSISTENCY_CHECKER and CONSISTENCY_CHECKS. Setting CONSISTENCY_CHECKS=0 disables the checker entirely.' Default retry is 5 when bypassing.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review pipeline environment variable configuration for CONSISTENCY_CHECKS and BYPASS_CONSISTENCY_CHECKER settings. Flag production pipelines with checker disabled or set to zero without documented approval.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag production CI/CD pipelines where CONSISTENCY_CHECKS=0 or BYPASS_CONSISTENCY_CHECKER is set without a documented exception.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Confirm the consistency checker is enabled in production Terraform pipelines.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review all Genesys Cloud Terraform pipelines for CONSISTENCY_CHECKS and BYPASS_CONSISTENCY_CHECKER settings. Ensure the checker is not disabled in production apply stages. Document rationale for any environment where it is disabled and confirm errors are captured to file and reviewed post-run.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Enabling the checker in pipelines that previously bypassed it may surface failures that were previously swallowed; investigate before enforcing.
evidence_examples: Pipeline env var export showing CONSISTENCY_CHECKS value
Terraform apply log showing consistency retry behavior
catalog.sample_bad_state: CONSISTENCY_CHECKS=0 in all environments; intermittent apply failures pass silently.
catalog.sample_good_state: Consistency checker active with default retries in production; disabled only in sandboxes with documented rationale.
catalog.review_cadence: Per pipeline configuration change and quarterly
catalog.false_positive_notes: Local developer or sandbox environments may intentionally disable the checker for faster iteration.
exceptions: Local developer testing environments with documented exception.

catalog.title: Use PKCE or implicit grant for browser-based SDK authentication
catalog.summary: Browser applications using the Genesys Cloud JavaScript SDK must authenticate via PKCE or implicit grant; client credentials must never be used in browser context.
catalog.why_it_matters: Client credentials (OAuth client ID + secret) cannot be kept confidential in browser applications because JavaScript source is fully readable to any end user. Embedding secrets in browser code exposes the OAuth credential to everyone who visits the application.
catalog.recommended_state: Browser applications use PKCE Grant (preferred) or Implicit Grant. Client credentials are used only in server-side or Node.js environments where the secret is never sent to the browser.
catalog.anti_pattern: Genesys Cloud SDK initialized with client credentials (client ID and secret) directly in browser JavaScript.
catalog.source_notes: JavaScript SDK README: 'This is restricted intentionally because it is impossible for client credentials to be handled securely in a browser application.' PKCE requires Node 18+ for code verifier/challenge helpers. Browser-supported grants: PKCE and Implicit.
catalog.detection_strategy: Code review and static analysis for SDK initialization in browser application code using client credentials grant type. Flag any production browser app that stores or transmits OAuth client secrets to the browser.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag browser application source files containing OAuth client secret initialization or explicit client credentials grant usage.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Replace client credentials in browser apps with PKCE grant.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Identify all browser applications using the Genesys Cloud SDK. Migrate to PKCE grant (preferred). Revoke and rotate any client secrets that may have been exposed in client-side code. Update OAuth client configuration to restrict grant type. Node 18+ is required for built-in PKCE helper methods.
catalog.rollback_considerations: PKCE requires session management changes; test thoroughly in staging before removing client credentials from browser code.
evidence_examples: SDK initialization using loginWithPKCE() instead of loginWithClientCredentials()
Browser app source confirming no embedded OAuth secret
catalog.sample_bad_state: Browser SPA initializes Genesys Cloud SDK with hardcoded client ID and secret using client credentials grant.
catalog.sample_good_state: Browser SPA authenticates via PKCE; client secret never reaches the browser.
catalog.review_cadence: Per release and quarterly security review
catalog.false_positive_notes: Server-side rendering or backend-for-frontend patterns may legitimately use client credentials server-side while serving browser clients.
exceptions: Server-side rendering contexts where credentials are held server-side and never exposed to the browser.

catalog.title: Do not use preview APIs in production integrations
catalog.summary: Preview APIs in the Genesys Cloud SDK and platform are subject to breaking and non-breaking changes at any time without notice and must not be relied upon in production systems.
catalog.why_it_matters: Preview APIs may change schema, alter behavior, or be removed without deprecation notice, causing silent production failures or integration breaks during routine platform updates.
catalog.recommended_state: All production integrations use only generally available (GA) API endpoints and SDK methods. Preview API usage is confined to sandbox or proof-of-concept environments with explicit tracking.
catalog.anti_pattern: Production integration calls preview-tagged API endpoints or SDK methods whose stability is not guaranteed.
catalog.source_notes: JavaScript SDK README: 'Preview APIs are included in this SDK. These resources are subject to both breaking and non-breaking changes at any time without notice.' Applications should not depend on preview API stability.
catalog.detection_strategy: Scan integration code and API call logs for SDK methods or endpoint paths flagged as preview or beta. Cross-reference against Genesys Cloud API changelog and SDK release notes.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag production integrations calling preview-tagged SDK methods or API endpoint paths containing a preview or beta segment.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Remove or replace all preview API usages in production integrations.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Audit all production integrations against the SDK documentation and API changelog. Identify any preview-flagged endpoints in active use. Replace with GA equivalents where available. Document remaining preview usages in a risk register with planned GA migration dates.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Replacing preview endpoints may require schema or behavior adjustments; validate in staging.
evidence_examples: SDK call stack identifying preview-tagged API method
API path containing /preview/ URL segment or preview annotation
catalog.sample_bad_state: Production integration uses a preview messaging API that is removed in a platform update, causing silent failures.
catalog.sample_good_state: All production API calls use GA endpoints; preview usage isolated to sandbox with tracking ticket.
catalog.review_cadence: Per release and after major platform updates
catalog.false_positive_notes: Sandbox environments testing upcoming features may intentionally use preview APIs.
exceptions: Documented proof-of-concept or sandbox environments with no production customer traffic.

catalog.title: Keep Genesys Cloud SDK versions current
catalog.summary: Production applications should track the latest or near-latest Genesys Cloud SDK version. SDK security patches and compatibility fixes are only released for the current version.
catalog.why_it_matters: Running stale SDK versions means security patches, API compatibility updates, and enum deserialization fixes are not received. Outdated SDKs may silently mishandle new platform schema changes or map unknown values to error states.
catalog.recommended_state: Production applications run on the latest or latest-minus-one major SDK version. SDK version is reviewed at each major platform update cycle.
catalog.anti_pattern: Production applications pinned to an SDK version multiple major releases behind, missing security and compatibility fixes.
catalog.source_notes: Python SDK README: 'it is strongly recommended that all applications using this SDK are kept up to date and use the latest version of the SDK.' Patches are released only for the latest version. Unknown enum values from newer API responses are mapped to 'outdated_sdk_version' rather than failing.
catalog.detection_strategy: Compare SDK version dependencies in application package manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, pom.xml, etc.) against the latest published version on the relevant package registry.
required_inputs: SDK release history from package registry
catalog.logic_hint: Flag applications pinned to SDK versions more than 2 major versions behind the current published release.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Update SDK dependencies to the latest or near-latest version.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Audit all production integrations for SDK version currency. Prioritize updates for integrations with known compatibility warnings. Test upgrades in staging before deploying to production. Establish a regular SDK update cadence tied to the Genesys Cloud platform release calendar.
catalog.rollback_considerations: SDK major version upgrades may contain breaking changes; test comprehensively and review release notes.
evidence_examples: package.json or requirements.txt showing current SDK version
Dependency audit report comparing installed vs. latest version
catalog.sample_bad_state: Node.js integration uses platform-client-sdk-javascript v142 while current version is v215; unknown enum responses map to 'outdated_sdk_version'.
catalog.sample_good_state: SDK dependency tracks within one major version of the latest published release; update reviewed quarterly.
catalog.review_cadence: Quarterly and after major platform updates
catalog.false_positive_notes: Integrations in active feature freeze may defer SDK updates to next planned sprint.
exceptions: Short-term deferral during active feature freeze with a scheduled update ticket.

catalog.title: Do not enable SDK request or response body logging in production without PII controls
catalog.summary: SDK-level request and response body logging must be disabled by default in production. When enabled for diagnostics, PII-scrubbing controls and time-bounded duration are required.
catalog.why_it_matters: Genesys Cloud API request and response bodies frequently contain customer PII including names, phone numbers, and account data. Persistent body logging without controls creates PII exposure in log aggregation systems, SIEM pipelines, and cloud storage.
catalog.recommended_state: Request and response body logging is disabled in production SDK configuration. When temporarily enabled for diagnostics, PII-masking controls are applied and the logging window is time-bounded and documented.
catalog.anti_pattern: SDK request and response body logging enabled persistently in production without PII controls, writing customer data to log aggregation or monitoring systems.
catalog.source_notes: JavaScript SDK: 'Be mindful that request and response bodies may contain PII — explicitly enable log_request_body and log_response_body only when necessary.' Python SDK: 'By default, the request and response bodies are not logged because these can contain PII.' Both READMEs note developer responsibility for log file rotation.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect production integration source code and deployment configuration for log_request_body or log_response_body settings enabled outside of sandbox contexts.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag production configurations with log_request_body or log_response_body set to true without documented PII risk acceptance and compensating controls.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Disable body logging in production or apply PII masking when enabled.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review all production integrations for SDK logging configuration. Disable request and response body logging by default. If diagnostic body logging is required, implement PII field masking, restrict log destination access, limit retention, and set a time-bound duration. Document all approved exceptions.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Disabling diagnostic logging may require alternative debug approaches; plan before disabling.
evidence_examples: SDK logging config export showing body logging disabled in production
Log masking configuration for approved time-bounded diagnostic sessions
catalog.sample_bad_state: Python integration has log_response_body=True in production config, writing customer names and phone numbers to CloudWatch Logs.
catalog.sample_good_state: Body logging disabled by default in production; enabled briefly in sandbox with PII masking enabled for debug sessions.
catalog.review_cadence: Per deployment and quarterly security review
catalog.false_positive_notes: Development and sandbox environments with no real customer data may legitimately enable body logging.
exceptions: Sandbox or development environments confirmed to have no real customer data.

catalog.title: Subscribe to Genesys Cloud system status notifications for your AWS region
catalog.summary: Operations teams must subscribe to regional Genesys Cloud system status alerts to receive timely awareness of platform incidents.
catalog.why_it_matters: Without proactive notification, incidents affecting the deployment region go undetected until users escalate problems, significantly increasing mean time to response and reducing platform trust.
catalog.recommended_state: At least one responsible operations contact is subscribed to status alerts for all Genesys Cloud AWS regions in which the organization is deployed.
catalog.anti_pattern: No subscription to platform status alerts; incident awareness depends entirely on user complaint escalation.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud Step 4 Onboarding Best Practices: 'Subscribe to AWS region status: Monitor the Genesys Cloud System Status page for incident alerts specific to your instance's region.'
catalog.detection_strategy: Verify that the operations runbook or on-call contact list includes a system status subscription entry for the organization's deployed AWS region. Confirm subscription is active and routes to an on-call group.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag organizations with no documented Genesys Cloud system status subscription or equivalent proactive notification mechanism.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Subscribe the operations team to Genesys Cloud status alerts for your AWS region.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Navigate to the Genesys Cloud System Status page and subscribe to notifications for the relevant AWS region(s). Route the subscription to the operations on-call group or NOC distribution list. Add the status page URL to the incident response runbook. Review subscription health annually.
catalog.rollback_considerations: No rollback risk; status subscriptions are additive and non-disruptive.
evidence_examples: Confirmed status subscription notification email or webhook
Runbook entry with status page URL and subscriber list
catalog.sample_bad_state: Organization has no proactive platform status monitoring; all incidents discovered via user-reported tickets.
catalog.sample_good_state: Operations team receives email or webhook alerts from Genesys Cloud status page within minutes of a regional incident declaration.
catalog.review_cadence: Annually and after any incident that lacked proactive detection
catalog.false_positive_notes: Organizations using independent synthetic monitoring as primary detection may have equivalent coverage without direct status subscriptions.
exceptions: Organizations with documented independent synthetic monitoring providing equivalent proactive coverage.

catalog.title: Define explicit failure paths for all failable actions in Architect flows
catalog.summary: Every action in an Architect flow that exposes a failure output connector must have an intentional, tested failure path rather than an unconnected terminal.
catalog.why_it_matters: Undefined failure paths in Architect flows result in stuck interactions, silent routing failures, or caller experience dead-ends. Failure handling is a production quality gate; callers should always reach a graceful outcome.
catalog.recommended_state: All flow actions with failure output connectors (data actions, transfer actions, Get/Set actions) have explicit, tested failure paths that route interactions to a recovery outcome or a live agent.
catalog.anti_pattern: Data actions, transfer actions, or decision branches with unconnected failure output connectors, causing interactions to stall or terminate abruptly.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud smart use cases and best practices documentation emphasizes that failure path handling in automated workflows is a critical design requirement. All automated flows should have defined failure outcomes.
catalog.detection_strategy: Export flow YAML or JSON. Identify all actions with available failure output connectors and flag those where the failure connector is unconnected or routes to a terminal action without logging or a recovery message.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag flow actions where the failure output connector is null, unconnected, or wired directly to a disconnect action without an intermediary recovery step.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Wire explicit failure paths to recovery actions for all failable flow actions.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review all Architect flows and inspect each action for available failure connectors. Connect failure paths to appropriate handlers: play a recovery message, offer a callback, or transfer to a live agent queue. Log the failure state with a Set Variable or Log action. Test each failure path in sandbox before publishing to production.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Adding failure paths changes flow logic; publish to test environment and validate before promoting to production.
evidence_examples: Flow YAML showing failure connector wired to a recovery state
Test run evidence demonstrating failure path trigger and recovery outcome
catalog.sample_bad_state: CRM data action in IVR flow has unconnected failure connector; caller hears silence and disconnects after action timeout.
catalog.sample_good_state: All data actions have failure paths leading to a recovery message followed by transfer to a live agent queue.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Simple utility flows with no external dependencies and no customer-facing interactions may have trivially low failure risk.
exceptions: Internal-only utility flows with no external data actions, transfers, or customer interactions.

catalog.title: Enforce multi-factor authentication for all Genesys Cloud administrators
catalog.summary: MFA must be configured and enforced for all users holding administrative or elevated roles in Genesys Cloud.
catalog.why_it_matters: Administrative accounts without MFA are highly vulnerable to credential-based attacks. A compromised admin account can modify routing, export contact data, disable security controls, or grant elevated access across the entire organization.
catalog.recommended_state: All users holding Master Admin or elevated custom roles have MFA enforced, preferably through SSO with mandatory MFA policy.
catalog.anti_pattern: Administrative users authenticate with username and password only, with no MFA or SSO enforcement.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud Security, Privacy, and Compliance Portal and onboarding documentation consistently list MFA enforcement for administrative roles as a baseline security control. SSO with enforced MFA is the recommended pattern.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect identity provider MFA enforcement policy and Genesys Cloud user MFA enrollment status for all users with Master Admin or elevated custom roles. Flag those without active MFA or SSO enrollment.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag users with Master Admin or elevated admin roles who do not have MFA enrolled or who are not covered by an SSO policy enforcing MFA.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Enforce MFA via SSO policy on all administrative accounts.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Audit MFA enrollment for all Master Admin and elevated custom role holders. Configure the identity provider to require MFA for those role populations. Implement SSO with mandatory MFA as the preferred approach. Remove MFA exemptions except for documented break-glass accounts with compensating controls and monitored usage.
catalog.rollback_considerations: MFA enforcement may lock out users who have not completed enrollment; communicate and stage rollout with a remediation period.
evidence_examples: Identity provider MFA enforcement policy configuration
User MFA enrollment status report filtered to admin roles
catalog.sample_bad_state: Master Admin users log in with email and password only; no MFA configured or required.
catalog.sample_good_state: All admin accounts require SSO with enforced MFA; break-glass accounts are physically secured and access is monitored.
catalog.review_cadence: Monthly enrollment audit and quarterly policy review
catalog.false_positive_notes: Non-interactive OAuth service accounts using client credentials grant legitimately do not use MFA.
exceptions: Non-interactive OAuth service accounts using client credentials grant with no human login.

catalog.title: Keep Architect flow size below the publish threshold
catalog.summary: Flow size must remain below 98% or the flow cannot be published. At 100% it cannot even be saved. Consolidate actions and use common modules to keep flows within limits.
catalog.why_it_matters: Flows at or above the publish threshold block emergency changes and force disruptive refactoring under pressure. Genesys Cloud enforces hard limits where neither save nor publish is possible at 100% utilization.
catalog.recommended_state: Production flows are kept below 70% size utilization (the red-warning threshold), providing headroom for growth and emergency changes.
catalog.anti_pattern: Flow grows unchecked until it breaches the 70% red warning or the 98% publish-blocked threshold, requiring emergency refactoring.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud Architect flow size documentation defines thresholds: <30% = none, 30% = yellow, 70% = red, 98% = cannot publish (can save), 100% = cannot save (export only). Consolidating multiple Update Data actions and using common module flows are the primary size-reduction strategies. Common module flows have a lower limit than other flow types.
catalog.detection_strategy: Export flow metadata and check the size indicator. Flag flows at or above 70% utilization. Identify flows with multiple consecutive Update Data actions that could be consolidated.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag flows with size utilization at or above 70%. Flag flows with three or more consecutive Update Data actions as consolidation candidates.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Refactor large flows: consolidate Update Data actions and extract reusable logic into common module flows.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Check flow size using the Architect flow size indicator. Consolidate multiple consecutive Update Data actions into single multi-statement actions. Extract repeated logic blocks into common module flows. Use variables to pass values instead of duplicating similar action instances. For very large flows, consider splitting into sub-flows via Transfer to Flow.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Refactoring requires testing in a sandbox before publishing to production.
evidence_examples: Flow size indicator at 70%+ showing red warning
Before/after Update Data action consolidation diff
catalog.sample_bad_state: Flow is at 95% size utilization; a recent feature addition would push it past the publish threshold.
catalog.sample_good_state: Flow is kept below 70% utilization; reusable logic is extracted into common modules.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Newly scaffolded complex flows may legitimately start large during initial development.
exceptions: New flows under active initial development that have not yet reached production.

catalog.title: Provide at least 20–30 training examples per bot intent
catalog.summary: Architect NLU bot intents should have a minimum of 20–30 diverse utterance examples to produce reliable intent classification.
catalog.why_it_matters: Intents trained on fewer than 20 examples produce unreliable classification, causing misrouting and poor containment rates. The NLU model requires sufficient example diversity to generalize across real caller utterances.
catalog.recommended_state: Each intent has 20–30 distinct utterance examples covering the breadth of expected caller phrasing.
catalog.anti_pattern: Intents trained on 5–10 examples producing high misclassification rates and escalations.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud bot building best practices: 'Provide at least 20–30 typical examples per intent.' Best practice recommends 15–30 examples. Target coverage of 99% of the most common cases. Start with the smallest, highest-priority intent list and grow iteratively.
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect bot intent configuration and count utterance examples per intent. Flag intents below the 20-example threshold.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag any NLU intent configured with fewer than 20 utterance examples.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Add diverse utterance examples until each intent has at least 20.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review each intent's utterance count. Add paraphrases, regional variants, and alternative phrasings until reaching 20–30 examples. Prioritize real caller utterances from Learning Panel data. Avoid adding all Learning Panel data indiscriminately — select only representative, correctly classified examples to prevent model bias.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Retraining the NLU model may change classification behavior for other intents; test in sandbox and review classification report before publishing.
evidence_examples: Intent configuration export showing utterance count per intent
NLU test report showing classification accuracy per intent
catalog.sample_bad_state: Intent 'MakePayment' has 6 utterance examples; frequent misclassification causes caller frustration.
catalog.sample_good_state: All intents have 20–30 varied utterance examples covering expected caller phrasings.
catalog.review_cadence: Per bot publish and when classification accuracy drops
catalog.false_positive_notes: Binary confirmation intents (e.g., yes/no) may require fewer examples than open-ended classification intents.
exceptions: Simple yes/no confirmation intents with constrained vocabulary.

catalog.title: Create dedicated queues per media type for workitem routing
catalog.summary: Workitem queues should be dedicated to a single media type. Mixed-media queues allow workitem priority to displace voice and other interaction types unexpectedly.
catalog.why_it_matters: When workitems share a queue with voice or digital interactions, high-priority workitems can preempt real-time interactions such as inbound calls, causing unintended service level degradation for voice customers.
catalog.recommended_state: Each workitem queue handles a single media type. Voice, digital, and workitem interactions are routed through separate, dedicated queues.
catalog.anti_pattern: A single queue serves both voice ACD calls and workitems, causing priority conflicts that sideline real-time voice interactions.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud workitem assignment best practices: 'Create queues that are dedicated to each media type. When you create queues with mixed media, priority of workitems can sideline other interactions, such as a voice call.'
catalog.detection_strategy: Inspect queue configuration for queues that have both workitem and non-workitem (voice or digital) media types assigned. Flag mixed-media queues serving workitems.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag queues configured to receive both workitem interactions and voice or digital ACD interactions.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Separate workitem routing to dedicated workitem-only queues.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Audit all queues handling workitems. Identify any queue also receiving voice or digital ACD interactions. Create dedicated workitem queues and migrate workitem routing rules. Verify that voice and digital service levels are not affected after the change.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Queue separation changes routing configuration; validate in staging and monitor service levels post-change.
evidence_examples: Queue media type configuration export showing single media type per queue
Service level report before/after workitem queue separation
catalog.sample_bad_state: Single queue serves both inbound voice calls and high-priority workitems; voice SLA degrades during workitem surges.
catalog.sample_good_state: Separate queues for voice ACD, digital, and workitem interactions; each with independent priority and service level thresholds.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Very small deployments with no workitem volume may have minimal practical impact from mixed queues.
exceptions: Lab or low-volume pilot environments with no production SLA requirements.

catalog.title: Use the async analytics endpoint for large historical conversation queries
catalog.summary: Historical analytics queries for large result sets or data older than a few days should use the async conversation details endpoint, not the synchronous endpoint.
catalog.why_it_matters: The synchronous analytics endpoint is limited to 100,000 records per query and is subject to timeout. Large historical queries using the synchronous path create unnecessary latency and can fail silently, while the async endpoint handles large datasets reliably.
catalog.recommended_state: Integrations performing historical analytics queries use the async endpoint (/api/v2/analytics/conversations/details/jobs) for datasets expected to exceed synchronous limits or covering extended date ranges.
catalog.anti_pattern: Historical reporting integration uses the synchronous analytics endpoint for multi-week date ranges, hitting the 100,000 record cap and receiving truncated results without error.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud analytics API documentation: conversation detail endpoint max records per query is 100,000. Query interval start date limit is 558 days in the past. For historical queries, use the async endpoint (/api/v2/analytics/conversations/details/jobs). For recent data, use the notifications service when possible.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review integration code for analytics query patterns. Flag integrations querying date ranges spanning more than 7 days or expected volumes exceeding 100,000 records using the synchronous endpoint.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag synchronous analytics queries spanning more than 7 days or where estimated result set exceeds 100,000 records.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Switch large historical analytics queries to the async endpoint.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Identify integrations that query conversation analytics over extended date ranges. Migrate them to the async jobs endpoint (/api/v2/analytics/conversations/details/jobs). Implement job polling with status checks and result pagination. Prefer time-bounded sub-queries to keep datasets manageable.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Async endpoint requires different response handling; test error and timeout scenarios before deploying.
evidence_examples: Integration code showing async job submission and result polling
API call log comparing synchronous truncation with async full result
catalog.sample_bad_state: Reporting integration queries 6 months of conversation data synchronously, consistently receiving exactly 100,000 records (truncated) with no error.
catalog.sample_good_state: Historical queries use the async job endpoint; results are paginated and complete.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Short time-window queries with low volume are appropriate for the synchronous endpoint.
exceptions: Queries covering less than 7 days with expected volume well below 100,000 records.

catalog.title: Subscribe to campaign notification topics instead of polling for stop state
catalog.summary: Integrations waiting for an outbound campaign to stop should subscribe to the campaign notification topic (v2.outbound.campaigns.{id}) rather than polling the campaign API.
catalog.why_it_matters: Campaign stop takes an indeterminate amount of time. Polling adds unnecessary request volume and is explicitly discouraged by Genesys. The notification service provides real-time state change events with no polling overhead.
catalog.recommended_state: Integrations that need to react to campaign state transitions subscribe to the campaign notification topic and trigger on the event.
catalog.anti_pattern: Integration polls GET /api/v2/outbound/campaigns/{id} every few seconds waiting for status to become 'off', generating hundreds of unnecessary requests per stop cycle.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud Contact Management developer documentation: 'use the notification service to subscribe to the campaign's topic (v2.outbound.campaigns.{id}) to raise an event when the campaign's state changes' — polling is NOT recommended since stopping takes indeterminate time.
catalog.detection_strategy: Review integration code for polling loops against the GET campaign status endpoint. Flag any implementation that polls campaign state rather than subscribing to the notification topic.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag integrations with repeated calls to GET /api/v2/outbound/campaigns/{id} within short time windows, indicative of state polling.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Subscribe to the campaign notification topic (v2.outbound.campaigns.{id}) instead of polling.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Identify all integrations that poll for campaign state changes. Implement WebSocket notification channel subscription to v2.outbound.campaigns.{id}. Handle state-change events to trigger downstream logic. Remove the polling loop. Retain a fallback re-check only on WebSocket reconnect.
catalog.rollback_considerations: WebSocket notification requires channel management and reconnect handling; test connection recovery scenarios.
evidence_examples: Integration code showing notification channel subscription and event handler
Removal of polling loop from campaign stop workflow
catalog.sample_bad_state: Integration polls campaign status every 3 seconds for up to 10 minutes after issuing a stop command.
catalog.sample_good_state: Integration subscribes to v2.outbound.campaigns.{id} and receives a stop-state event within seconds of campaign completion.
catalog.false_positive_notes: A single status check after issuing a stop command (non-looping) is acceptable as a confirmation step.
exceptions: One-time status confirmation check (not a polling loop) immediately after a stop command.

catalog.title: Stay within Genesys Cloud concurrent campaign and CPS limits
catalog.summary: Outbound deployments must be designed within published Genesys Cloud platform limits: 50 concurrent voice campaigns, 25 digital, 15 CPS org-wide, and 50 CPS per campaign.
catalog.why_it_matters: Exceeding platform limits causes campaign failures, throttling, or edge capacity exhaustion. Planning campaign schedules without awareness of these limits creates production incidents.
catalog.recommended_state: Campaign schedules are designed with awareness of concurrent limits. CPS is tracked and managed proactively. Edge capacity is verified against concurrent outbound line requirements.
catalog.anti_pattern: Multiple business units independently schedule outbound campaigns without coordination, collectively exceeding the 50 concurrent voice campaign limit or 15 CPS org-wide limit.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud outbound dialer limitations: voice campaigns max 50 concurrent, digital max 25, skills-based max 5; org CPS limit 15, per-campaign CPS limit 50 (effective March 2025); contact list max 1M contacts; DNC records per org max 2M; lines per Edge 300–350.
catalog.detection_strategy: Monitor concurrent running campaign count and aggregate CPS across all active campaigns. Flag when concurrent count approaches 80% of platform limits or when CPS is within 20% of the org ceiling.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag organizations with more than 40 concurrently running voice campaigns (80% of 50 limit) or aggregate CPS approaching 12+ (80% of 15 limit).
catalog.recommended_action_short: Stagger campaign schedules to stay within concurrent and CPS limits.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Inventory all active campaigns and their run windows. Calculate peak concurrent count and aggregate CPS. Stagger campaign start times to distribute load. Review Edge line capacity (300–350 lines per Edge) against concurrent outbound line requirements. Escalate capacity concerns to Genesys Support if limits require adjustment.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Rescheduling active campaigns may disrupt ongoing contact attempts; plan changes during non-peak windows.
evidence_examples: Campaign schedule showing concurrent run windows
Outbound metrics showing CPS trend vs. org limit
catalog.sample_bad_state: 52 voice campaigns active simultaneously; campaign failures occur silently as limit is breached.
catalog.sample_good_state: Campaign schedules are staggered to keep concurrent count below 40 and aggregate CPS below 12.
catalog.review_cadence: Monthly and during campaign planning cycles
catalog.false_positive_notes: Short-duration campaigns that start and stop quickly may briefly overlap without operational impact.
exceptions: Temporary short-overlap windows during staggered starts that resolve within minutes.

catalog.title: Enforce MFA for SSO users at the identity provider, not Genesys Cloud
catalog.summary: Users authenticating via SSO do not receive MFA prompts from Genesys Cloud — MFA enforcement for SSO users must be configured at the identity provider (IdP) level.
catalog.why_it_matters: Organizations relying on Genesys Cloud's MFA for SSO-authenticated users will have a false sense of security: Genesys Cloud does not challenge SSO users for a second factor. If MFA is not enforced at the IdP, SSO-authenticated admins are protected by password only.
catalog.recommended_state: The IdP enforces MFA for all users who access Genesys Cloud, particularly those with administrative roles. Genesys Cloud org-level MFA is applied to native login users. Both paths are covered.
catalog.anti_pattern: Organization assumes Genesys Cloud MFA settings apply to SSO users. SSO users bypass MFA entirely because neither Genesys nor the IdP enforces a second factor for the Genesys application.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud MFA documentation explicitly states: 'MFA applies to native login only — SSO users do NOT receive MFA prompts from Genesys. Administrators authenticating via SSO already require MFA from their identity provider.' Mandatory MFA for specific admin permissions took effect March 9, 2026.
catalog.detection_strategy: Verify IdP MFA policy configuration for the Genesys Cloud application/SAML assertion. Confirm that MFA is required for users with Genesys administrative roles. Flag SSO configurations without IdP-enforced MFA for the Genesys Cloud relying party.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag organizations using SSO without a documented IdP-enforced MFA policy covering the Genesys Cloud application.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Configure MFA enforcement for Genesys Cloud at the identity provider, not only in Genesys Cloud settings.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review the IdP application policy for the Genesys Cloud SAML/OIDC integration. Enforce MFA at the IdP level for all users accessing Genesys Cloud, with particular priority for users holding administrative roles. Verify the enforcement through a test authentication. Document the MFA coverage for both native login and SSO paths.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Adding IdP MFA may disrupt users who have not enrolled a second factor; communicate and allow an enrollment grace period.
evidence_examples: IdP application policy showing MFA required for Genesys Cloud
Test authentication showing MFA challenge for SSO users
catalog.sample_bad_state: SSO is configured but IdP does not require MFA for Genesys Cloud. Admins log in with SSO and password only.
catalog.sample_good_state: IdP enforces MFA for Genesys Cloud; native login also has MFA enabled. All authentication paths are MFA-protected.
catalog.review_cadence: Quarterly and after any IdP policy change
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some organizations use a global IdP MFA policy covering all applications, which satisfies this requirement.
exceptions: IdP with a global MFA policy that includes Genesys Cloud without an application-specific rule.

catalog.title: Configure SIP trunk groups in active/active mode, not active/passive
catalog.summary: Genesys recommends active/active load balancing for SIP trunk groups on BYOC Premises Edges. Each Edge should have a dedicated outbound SIP trunk to the PSTN provider.
catalog.why_it_matters: Active/passive trunk groups leave one Edge idle during normal operation, wasting capacity and creating longer failover lag. Active/active distributes load evenly and uses all available trunk capacity, while a dedicated trunk per Edge ensures provider-level redundancy.
catalog.recommended_state: SIP trunk groups are configured in active/active mode. Each Edge appliance has a dedicated outbound SIP trunk to the PSTN provider.
catalog.anti_pattern: SIP trunk group configured active/passive, leaving secondary Edge trunk idle and creating slower failover with no load distribution.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Edge redundancy documentation: 'Genesys recommends active/active load balancing on SIP trunk groups (not active/passive)' and 'Genesys recommends working with the PSTN provider to build a dedicated outbound SIP trunk to each Edge appliance.'
catalog.detection_strategy: Review SIP trunk group configuration for each site and verify that active/active load balancing is selected. Verify that each Edge appliance has a dedicated outbound SIP trunk.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag trunk groups configured in active/passive mode or sites where a single trunk serves multiple Edge appliances.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Switch SIP trunk groups to active/active and provision dedicated per-Edge trunks.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review all site trunk group configurations. Change active/passive groups to active/active where the PSTN provider supports it. Work with the provider to provision a dedicated outbound SIP trunk for each Edge appliance. Verify load distribution and failover behavior after changes.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Trunk group reconfiguration requires planned change window with PSTN provider coordination.
evidence_examples: Trunk group configuration export showing active/active setting
Per-Edge trunk provisioning confirmation from PSTN provider
catalog.sample_bad_state: SIP trunk group active/passive; primary Edge handles all calls while secondary sits idle with no load sharing.
catalog.sample_good_state: Active/active trunk group distributes load across all Edges; each Edge has its own dedicated PSTN trunk.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Some PSTN providers do not support active/active SIP trunk configuration; verify provider capability first.
exceptions: PSTN providers that technically cannot support active/active trunk configuration.

catalog.title: Use Queue ID for conditional logic in agent scripts, not Queue Name
catalog.summary: Agent scripts performing conditional logic on the current queue should reference the Queue ID (Scripter.Queue ID) rather than the Queue Name to avoid unnecessary platform data requests.
catalog.why_it_matters: Referencing Queue Name in script logic triggers a synchronous platform data request to resolve the name at runtime, adding latency. Queue ID is resolved without a platform round-trip. Queue names also change over time, while IDs remain stable.
catalog.recommended_state: Agent scripts use Scripter.Queue ID for conditional branching and queue-based logic.
catalog.anti_pattern: Script conditional checks compare Scripter.Queue Name, causing a hidden platform data request on every script load.
catalog.source_notes: Genesys Cloud scripting best practices: 'Use Scripter.Queue ID for conditional logic, not Scripter.Queue Name (Queue Name requires a platform data request).'
catalog.detection_strategy: Review agent script logic for conditional branches or comparisons referencing Scripter.Queue Name.
catalog.logic_hint: Flag agent scripts with conditional logic referencing Scripter.Queue Name instead of Scripter.Queue ID.
catalog.recommended_action_short: Replace Scripter.Queue Name with Scripter.Queue ID in conditional script logic.
catalog.recommended_action_detailed: Review all agent scripts for Queue Name references in conditional logic. Note the Queue ID for each applicable queue from the admin console. Replace Queue Name comparisons with Queue ID comparisons. Test the script to confirm correct behavior.
catalog.rollback_considerations: Script changes require validation before publishing; test in a sandbox environment.
evidence_examples: Script logic showing Scripter.Queue ID comparison
Before/after diff replacing Queue Name with Queue ID
catalog.sample_bad_state: Script uses 'if Scripter.Queue Name == Support Tier 1' — triggers hidden platform data request on every load.
catalog.sample_good_state: Script uses 'if Scripter.Queue ID == 8f3a2b...' — no platform round-trip required.
catalog.false_positive_notes: Display-only references to Queue Name in script UI labels do not carry the same performance impact.
exceptions: Queue Name references used only for display purposes in UI labels, not in conditional logic.
